title: Completed perfect realization is fully faithful and left adjoint to point sections
statement: Let D, l and E be as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with l different from the characteristic. There exists a functor from the bounded finitely generated derived-complete O_E module complexes of [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes] to integral constructible complexes on Spec(D.k), left adjoint to the specified integral fibre functor, whose adjunction unit is invertible at every object. No assertion about the counit on arbitrary integral constructible complexes is included.

source.place: Completed perfect realization is fully faithful and left adjoint to point sections; extracted from the point-fibre argument; lean/Sheaf/Paper/PointIntegralPerfectRealization.lean, pointIntegralPerfectRealization

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, $A_n=A/\pi^n$ and $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$. The coefficient DVR theorem makes $A$ a domain with every ideal principal, hence Noetherian, and with finite residue field. Choosing a finite set of residue representatives and successively writing $x=r_0+\pi x_1$ shows that every element of $A_n$ is represented by $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}r_j\pi^j$; thus $A_n$ is finite and Noetherian. The continuous-coefficient description, applied to the noetherian scheme $s$, identifies $\Gamma(s,B)$ canonically with $C(\{*\},A)=A$, preserving constants and all quotient projections. The completed-constant reduction theorem gives flatness of $B$ over $\underline A$ and $B\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline{A_n}\simeq\underline{A_n}$. Indeed the resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\pi^n}A]$ of $A_n$ becomes $[B\xrightarrow{\pi^n}B]$. Constant-sheaf exactness and this flatness make its negative cohomology zero. Exactness of sections therefore gives $\Gamma(s,\underline{A_n})=A_n$, with the canonical map from constant values as the identification. No identification of $B$ with the discrete constant sheaf $\underline A$ is made.

proof.text: For either $(R,\mathcal R)=(A_n,\underline{A_n})$ or $(A,B)$ define $L_{\mathcal R}(M)=\mathcal R\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ for an $R$-module $M$. Here constant sheaves and sheaf tensor products have exactly their existing definitions. There is an adjunction $L_{\mathcal R}\dashv\Gamma(s,-)$: a sheaf map $u:L_{\mathcal R}M\to F$ gives $m\mapsto u_s(1\otimes m)$; conversely $t:M\to F(s)$ gives, before sheafification, $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$ on every object $U$, and then extends uniquely to the sheaf tensor product. These constructions are inverse and natural; the balancing relation is precisely $R$-linearity of $t$. Constant sheafification is exact by the arbitrary-site module-sheafification theorem. Thus $L_{\underline{A_n}}$ is exact, and $L_B$ is exact by flatness in step 1. Both right adjoints are exact by the point-sections theorem. For any finitely presented $R$-module $M$, a presentation $R^a\to R^b\to M\to0$ and exactness give $\Gamma(s,L_{\mathcal R}M)\cong\operatorname{coker}(R^a\to R^b)=M$. On free generators this is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, so the isomorphism is precisely the adjunction unit, not an arbitrary identification.

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor derived factorization to the two exact adjoints in step 2. They act termwise, commute with every shift and preserve distinguished triangles. Their termwise unit and counit are chain maps; naturality makes them commute with differentials, and the two triangle identities hold degree by degree. They descend through the localization, with the same identities, to an adjunction on the unbounded derived categories. Exact-functor preservation of homology identifies the cohomology of the unit $M\to\Gamma(s,L_{\mathcal R}M)$ with the underived unit at $H^i(M)$. Consequently this derived unit is an isomorphism whenever all $H^i(M)$ are finitely presented, by the cohomological isomorphism criterion. In particular it is an isomorphism on $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_n)$ and on $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$: finite modules over the finite Noetherian ring $A_n$, and finitely generated modules over the Noetherian ring $A$, are finitely presented. This argument uses the descended termwise unit and counit themselves, so their normalization is fixed.

proof.text: Every bounded $A$-complex with finitely generated cohomology is perfect. To verify the needed hypotheses explicitly, take a finitely generated module $N$. The Noetherian finite-free-resolution theorem gives $A^{r_1}\to A^{r_0}\to N\to0$. Its kernel $J\subset A^{r_0}$ is finitely generated, being the image of the first finite free term, and is torsion free because $A$ is a domain and $A^{r_0}$ is torsion free. The finite torsion-free DVR theorem makes $J$ finite free. Thus $0\to J\to A^{r_0}\to N\to0$ is a bounded finite-free resolution. The perfect-cohomology assembly theorem now gives a bounded finite-projective representative $Q$ for every $M\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$. The argument includes $N=0$ and does not impose finite Tor dimension on modules over $A_n$; those rings may be singular.

For any bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $Q$, $L_BQ=B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline Q$ is in $D^b_c(s,A)$ by the integral stratified-perfect characterization, using its explicit comparison with the category of derived-complete integral coefficients in the statement. Its hypotheses hold: $s$ is noetherian, of dimension zero, and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$ because $\ell\ne p$; use the single stratum $s$ and the identity trivializing cover. This is its condition (ii), with the specified completed sheaf $B$. In particular this assertion includes completeness and the reductions required in the present definition, rather than silently identifying two integral categories. The reduction calculation of step 1 also gives $L_BQ\otimes_B^L\underline{A_n}\cong\underline{Q\otimes_A A_n}$: for a finite projective term take a direct summand of a finite free term and use the same quotient map. These reductions have bounded finite cohomology in the fixed term interval of $Q$, independent of $n$. Thus step 6 shows $L_B$ carries every object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ into the integral source. Point-sections finiteness carries the integral source into $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$. The adjunction of step 3 therefore restricts to these full subcategories, and its unit is an isomorphism there.

theorem pointIntegralPerfectRealization
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] :
    ∃ L : (DerivedCategory.pointFgComplete
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
        (Ideal.span {ULift.up (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)})).FullSubcategory ⥤
        sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k)),
      ∃ a : L ⊣ pointIntegralFibre D l hl E, ∀ M, IsIso (a.unit.app M)
